newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends lower in U.S. after mark/yen rally.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends lower in U.S. after mark/yen rally.

text.p: The dollar hit a fresh 33-month high against a slumping yen early Monday, but ended lower against major currencies.
The greenback held most of its overnight gains versus the yen, posted amid signs Japan will likely hold interest rates at historic lows.
But many observers now believe low German rates have hit bottom, which helped trigger a furious mark/yen rally and limit the dollar's advance, dealers said.
Low Japanese rates help the dollar against the yen, but higher German rates would hurt the dollar against the mark.
The yen fell across the board in overseas trade after Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party in general elections captured 239 of the 251 seats needed for a majority.
The win suggested Japan would keep its official discount rate at 0.5 percent, analysts said.
Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita later bolstered that perception, telling BOJ regional branch managers that his main monetary policy goal is securing an economic recovery.
Meanwhile, data showed German M3 money supply growth fell to 8.4 percent in September from 8.7 percent in August, which may allow the Bundesbank to keep interest rates steady.

"Most of the interest we saw was to buy marks against yen. As a result, the dollar was a little heavy against the mark, but higher against the yen," said Thomas Arnold, chief currency dealer at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.

The dollar ended at 112.71/76 yen, down from 112.81/84 at the open, after reaching 112.90 yen, the highest level since 113.58 in January 1994, in early trading. The dollar fell to 1.5342/45 marks from 1.5380/90 at the open.
Dealers said the greenback should rally toward 113 yen in coming sessions, aided by robust U.S. asset markets, while the yen suffers as oil-poor Japan struggles under high oil prices.
"There are a lot of things keeping the dollar well-bid against the yen," said Arnold.
The mark hit a six-week high at 73.49 yen and most other currencies also rallied as funds flowed out of Japan.
The New Zealand dollar hit an eight-year high at $0.7140, while the Australian dollar and sterling also rallied against the yen.

"The Japanese election presented not a stumbling block, but more of a temporary pause, and now there is a lot of interest to move money out of Japan," said Seth Garrett, chief currency dealer at CS First Boston.
Against the mark, the dollar suffered from profit-taking as investors cashed in after a sharp dollar rally over the last several weeks, dealers said.
The U.S. unit had risen nearly seven pfennigs in four weeks and some market players took an opportunity to book those handsome profits, dealers said.
"We saw some profit-taking in sterling and the dollar against the mark," Garrett said. "But I think we should find support soon and gradually resume the move back up."

In other trade, the dollar fell to 1.2625/35 Swiss francs from 1.2670/80 at the open. Sterling fell to $1.5924/29 from $1.5933/40. The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3464/69 from C$1.3495/00. The Australian dollar fell to $0.7966/71 from $0.7977/82.
--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
